title: Monotonicity of Answer Length
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, with oracle, input $x$, state predicate $G$, initial configuration $a$, and natural numbers $N\le N'$. Suppose every choice sequence of length $N$ from $a$ halts, and every earlier prefix configuration that is still active satisfies $G$. Then a length-$N'$ choice sequence from $a$ that leaves answer $b$ exists if and only if a length-$N$ choice sequence from $a$ that leaves answer $b$ exists, for either Boolean value $b$.
hypotheses_covered: machine A, oracle, input x, and state predicate G
natural numbers N and N′ with N ≤ N′
all length-N sequences halt from a
every active configuration along every shorter prefix satisfies G
